decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with left arm toward the purple nut; keep right arm parked. Slowly pitch the gripper downward above the table.
Finish orienting left gripper vertically and move above the purple nut. Estimated nut height and centering will be checked in wrist RGB before closing.
Lower the open left gripper toward the purple nut with a small visual centering correction. Stop above final grasp height to verify alignment.
Center the purple nut between left fingers, close fully, and lift slightly. Retention remains to be confirmed from the next wrist and head images.
Purple nut appears retained. Lift for clearance and carry it over the matching purple bolt in the left workspace without changing grasp orientation.
Lower the held purple nut toward the matching bolt with a small lateral correction; inspect concentricity before applying tightening rotation.
The purple bolt is visible through the held nut. Apply a small centering correction and a slow clockwise tightening stroke with minimal downward feed.
Wrist views suggest a small lateral offset rather than full engagement. Shift the held purple nut left toward the bolt axis, then finish a short clockwise seating stroke.
Release the purple nut on the bolt and reset wrist rotation with fingers open, avoiding the wrist joint limit. Check whether the nut stays supported and aligned.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lift clear, move to the fallen purple nut, and descend with fingers open.
Use wrist-image centering to recover the purple nut, close fully, and perform a short lift to verify retention before another insertion attempt.
Lift the recovered purple nut clear and realign above the purple screw. Use a higher inspection pose to avoid dragging the nut against the shaft.
Translate toward the visible purple shaft and lower cautiously. The recovered nut hangs slightly lower in the fingers, so stop higher than the prior insertion attempt.
The shaft is horizontally centered but remains above the bore in the wrist view. Lower the nut slowly to test engagement, with no tightening rotation yet.
The purple nut has tilted instead of seating. Lift it away from the shaft and move to clear table space for a stable regrasp rather than forcing insertion.
Set the tilted purple nut onto clear table space, release it, and lift the fingers to inspect its resting orientation for a centered regrasp.
The purple nut has settled upright and is centered in the wrist view. Descend to grasp its side flats, close, and lift to inspect whether it remains upright.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Reopen, move over the purple nut's observed location, and descend to inspect before closing.
Use the unobstructed wrist view to center the upright purple nut between open fingers and lower eight millimeters before grasping.
Close on the centered purple nut and lift vertically to verify an upright, stable grasp before moving back to the screw.
The purple nut now appears upright and retained. Lift for clearance and carry it above the purple screw using the revised visual axis estimate.
Center the upright nut over the shaft using wrist parallax, then descend slowly toward the thread start while maintaining the grasp.
The shaft is centered laterally but not entering the bore. Relieve contact slightly and test a small horizontal correction along the other table-plane direction instead of pushing downward.
The correction moved the shaft toward the bore. Refine along that direction, lower only a few millimeters, and test a short clockwise engagement stroke.
The purple tip is visible but slightly right of the bore. Correct that offset at the current wrist angle and continue a short clockwise stroke with very light axial feed.
Two wrist angles indicate the purple shaft is left of the current world position. Relieve contact, recenter using that estimate, and return to the same height without further twisting.
Keep height and wrist angle fixed while correcting the remaining image-depth offset along the table. Check the shaft against the nut bore before another tightening stroke.
The purple tip now appears inside the bore. Make a small final centering adjustment, then test a short clockwise seating stroke without approaching the wrist limit.
The nut still appears offset, not threaded. Lift clear while unwinding the wrist away from its limit, retaining the nut and returning over the visually estimated shaft axis.
Keep the shaft laterally centered and lower strictly vertically, isolating height from planar alignment. Stop to inspect before further rotation.
The shaft tip is appearing at the bore edge after vertical descent. Lower another small amount, then apply a short clockwise engagement stroke while keeping the gripper closed.
The purple shaft now fills the bore rather than showing table through it. Continue a controlled clockwise stroke, then open without translating to test whether the nut remains seated.
The released purple nut remains supported on its matching shaft. Reset the wrist with fingers open for another tightening stroke, leaving the assembly undisturbed.
Regrasp higher on the supported purple nut's side flats, then apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed.
Finish the current purple tightening stroke, release, and reset the wrist with fingers open. Keep the supported assembly at the same planar position.
Regrasp the supported purple nut and advance it with another clockwise stroke. The shaft is visibly centered and higher within the bore.
Release the purple nut and reset the wrist without undoing the threaded assembly. One more short tightening cycle is planned before moving to the other colors.
Apply a final controlled tightening stroke to the purple pair, then release the nut. Inspect its seated depth before withdrawing.
Withdraw open from the seated purple pair, unwind the wrist away from its limit, and approach the blue nut in the left workspace for transfer.
Approach the blue nut using the revised table-height estimate and wrist centering. Correct the small gripper tilt and stop above grasp height.
The blue nut is centered beneath the vertical gripper. Lower to its side flats, close fully, and lift vertically to confirm retention before transferring it.
The blue nut is upright and retained. Lift it clear and carry it toward a central staging spot for pickup by the right arm, keeping the arms separated.
Set the blue nut upright at the center staging location and release. The right arm remains parked until the left arm clears the transfer area.
Clear the left arm upward and back into its own workspace. Begin a slow elbow-up right-arm approach to the staged blue nut, keeping the arms separated.
Park the left arm clear of the center. Orient the right gripper vertically and approach the staged blue nut from the right at clearance height.
Center the right gripper over the staged blue nut while descending to a pregrasp height. Keep the left arm parked and clear.
Fine-center on the staged blue nut, descend to the grasp height, close the right gripper, and lift briefly to verify retention.
The blue nut is retained upright. Lift and carry it over the blue screw with the right arm; move the open left arm toward the gray nut at clearance height while maintaining separation.
Lower the held blue nut toward the blue shaft with visual centering corrections. Simultaneously bring the open left gripper to a pregrasp pose over the gray nut; maintain separate workspaces.
Fine-center and grasp the gray nut with the left arm, then lift slightly. Correct the blue nut's lateral offset and test a slow clockwise seating stroke with the right arm.
Continue tightening the centered blue nut, then release to check support. Carry the retained gray nut to the center staging position with the left arm, keeping clearance.
The blue nut tilted during the last stroke. Withdraw the open right gripper and restore a vertical approach for recovery. Set the gray nut upright at the center and release it.
The gray nut is staged upright. Clear the left arm and approach the fallen blue nut with the open, vertical right gripper for a stable regrasp.
Center on the fallen blue nut, lower to its side flats, close fully, and lift slightly to verify that it is retained upright.
The blue nut is retained upright again. Lift clear, move over the blue shaft, and approach from above. Park the left arm away from the central staging area.
The blue shaft is centered laterally. Descend strictly vertically to the thread start, then test a small clockwise turn while retaining the nut.
The blue shaft now fills the centered bore. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with light downward feed, then release in place to verify support.
The blue nut remains supported after release. Reset the wrist with fingers open and make a small centering correction for the next tightening grasp.
Regrasp the supported blue nut and advance it with another clockwise stroke, keeping the shaft centered and maintaining a small axial feed.
Release and reset the right wrist for another blue tightening stroke. Begin returning the empty left arm toward origin using a gradual elbow-up retreat.
Advance the supported blue nut with another clockwise stroke. Continue the empty left arm's gradual return toward its origin pose, maintaining configuration continuity.
Release the supported blue nut and reset the right wrist for further tightening. Make only a small final origin correction with the empty left arm.
Regrasp the upright blue nut and continue clockwise tightening with a small axial feed. Keep the left arm at origin.
Release the blue nut and reset the wrist with fingers open for a final tightening pass, preserving the assembly's planar alignment.
Finish the blue tightening pass and release in place. Keep the left arm parked at origin; the gray nut remains staged for the next pickup.
Withdraw open from the blue pair, reset wrist rotation, and approach the staged gray nut at clearance height from the right workspace.
Descend toward the staged gray nut with the right gripper open, making a small fore-aft correction. Stop above grasp height for wrist-image alignment.
Correct the remaining fore-aft offset over the gray nut, descend to its side flats, close, and lift briefly to verify an upright grasp.
The gray nut appears tilted in the grasp. Set it back down, release, and reposition the open gripper for a centered upright regrasp instead of attempting insertion while tilted.
The gray nut has settled upright. Descend with a small parallax-compensating correction, close on the side flats, and lift vertically to confirm a stable grasp.
The gray nut is retained upright. Lift clear and carry it toward its matching screw in the right workspace, keeping the left arm at origin.
Bring the held gray nut over the visible matching shaft, then descend cautiously to an inspection height while keeping the nut upright.
Refine the gray shaft's lateral alignment and lower slowly to the thread start, keeping the nut upright and avoiding rotation until the bore is centered.
The gray shaft is visible centrally through the bore. Apply a controlled clockwise seating stroke with light axial feed, then release in place to check that the nut stays supported.
The gray nut remains upright on its shaft after release. Reset the wrist with fingers open and make a small centering/height correction for a stable tightening regrasp.
Regrasp the upright, supported gray nut and continue clockwise tightening with minimal downward feed. Keep the left arm at origin.
